pr_title: Consistent response for starting basic license
pr_body:
The start basic license action returns an inconsistent response when a
basic license exists but a new basic license with different `maxNodes`
or `expiryDate` fields is started. In this case, the new license is
created but the response indicates that it was not. This PR makes the
response consistent.

Closes #86244
pr_comments: Hi @n1v0lg, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

There doesn't seem to be a way that a client would ever run into this issue because both `expiryDate` and `maxNodes` are static constants, so this is very minor indeed. Still good to be consistent though. I'm happy to merge this or to close the issue, either way.   

Can also add a test; haven't yet since our current restrictions make it quite difficult to start a second basic license with `expiryDate` or `maxNodes` values that differ from the presets.

> For unit test, can we just instanatiate or mock a License object for this purpose?

Absolutely, will add one since we are going ahead with this change 👍

@ywangd I went with including the test in `LicenceServiceTests` since it's consistent with the other tests already included in that test suite, and a "non-suprising" place for it to be. Testing `StartBasicClusterTask` would have made for a slightly easier setup but not by much (we'd still need the business of capturing the listener, generating or mocking an old license, etc).

issue_context.title: Start basic license response may be incorrect
issue_context.body:
For `POST _license/start_basic` the API, the system decides whether a new basic license should be generated using the following logic:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/3c15e4ebb1ae045d5cc690a0fd1e2f3c73173d39/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/license/StartBasicClusterTask.java#L101-L106

However, when building the response, the logic only takes account into old license type without checking maxNodes and expiryDate:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/3c15e4ebb1ae045d5cc690a0fd1e2f3c73173d39/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/license/StartBasicClusterTask.java#L64-L65

This means it is possible that client gets an error response of 
```json
{
  "acknowledged": true,
  "basic_was_started": false,
  "error_message": "Operation failed: Current license is basic."
}
```
while the license is actually generated successfully at the backend. 

See also: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/85993#discussion_r859356499

review_comments: We now also set the cluster name but that seems like a fair default and we get to re-use a bit of code
